title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (n° 6–7 of the notes). Fix an even length 2n. On the previous page Grothendieck builds a universal ring 𝔏, a free Z-module with basis φ_i^{β,α}. Here 0≤i≤n indexes the primitive degree, and α,β index the Lefschetz levels. The multiplication is that of matrix units: φ_i^{β,α}φ_{i'}^{β',α'} = 0 unless i=i' and the inner indices match, and otherwise it is again a matrix unit. So 𝔏 ≅ ∏_{i=0}^{n} M_{n-i+1}(Z). It is the integral endomorphism algebra of the 'universal Lefschetz graded module' ⊕_i ⊕_α L^α P^i. In this algebra live:
- L_0 = Σ φ_i^{α+1,α};
- Λ_0 = Σ φ_i^{α-1,α}. This is Grothendieck's integral Λ (L^αx ↦ L^{α-1}x for x primitive), not the sl₂-normalised dual.
- the degree projectors π_k and the bigraded projectors π_{i,α} (onto L^αP^i).
Their mutual relations are the formulas (6.14).

Proposition on this page. Let M* be a graded abelian group of length 2n and E a graded subring of End(M*) containing L ∈ E^2 and the degree projectors π_i. The following are equivalent:
- (i) M* satisfies the hard Lefschetz condition of the theorem of n° 6 (L^{n-i}: M^i → M^{2n-i} bijective), and the inverse operators, equivalently Λ, lie in E.
- (ii) There is a ring homomorphism φ: 𝔏 → E with φ(L_0)=L and φ(π_i)=π_i.
Moreover φ is then unique, and it sends Λ_0 to Λ, π_{i,α} to π_{i,α} and φ_i^{β,α} to the corresponding operators of n° 6. A marginal box marked 'conditions essentielles!' adds further equivalent conditions: (iii) existence of an auxiliary grading Σ^α compatible with the n° 6 conditions; (iv) a variant with a faithful module.

Proof.
- (i)⇒(ii): follows from the multiplication table of the φ_i^{β,α} given in n° 6 together with the theorem of n° 6. Under hard Lefschetz the primitive decomposition yields operators in E satisfying exactly the matrix-unit relations.
- (ii)⇒(i): in 𝔏 one has (Λ_0^{n-i}L_0^{n-i} − 1)π_i = 0 and (L_0^{n-i}Λ_0^{n-i} − 1)π_{2n-i} = 0. Applying φ and setting Λ = φ(Λ_0) gives the same identities in E. So L^{n-i} is invertible from degree i to degree 2n−i, with inverse Λ^{n-i} lying in E. This is condition (ii) of the n° 6 theorem.
- Uniqueness: once hard Lefschetz holds, Λ and the π_{i,α} are forced by L and the π_i through (6.14). Hence φ is determined on generators.

Purpose. This is an abstract, integral, 'representing object' formulation of the relation between the Lefschetz-type standard conjecture B (Λ algebraic) and the algebraicity of the inverse of hard Lefschetz, given the Künneth projectors (conjecture C). E plays the role of the ring of algebraic correspondences inside End(H*(X)). The next page draws a corollary for an arbitrary graded ring Σ: existence of u: Φ→Σ is equivalent to the existence of w_i with (w_iL^{n-i} − 1)π_{2n-i} = 0. It also shows by the case n=1 that L alone does not suffice; one must give L and the π_i together.
errors: The index range on the previous page reads 0≤α,β≤2n−i. For the matrix-unit description it should be 0≤α,β≤n−i (with 0≤i≤n), giving blocks of size n−i+1. This is probably a slip or an earlier convention.

The (ii)⇒(i) argument as written only shows that L^{n-i} has a two-sided inverse in E between degrees i and 2n−i. That L maps M^i into M^{i+2} (needed to speak of L^{n-i}: M^i→M^{2n-i}) also follows, since φ respects L_0π_i = π_{i+2}L_0, but this is not stated.
The proof of (i)⇒(ii) is only sketched (a reference to n° 6), and the marginal conditions (iii) and (iv) are left essentially unproved and only half-formulated.

ideas.what: Universal ring 𝔏 = free Z-module on matrix units φ_i^{β,α}, i.e. ∏_i M_{n-i+1}(Z), such that Lefschetz structures (L, π_i, Λ) on a graded module or ring are exactly homomorphisms out of 𝔏
ideas.modern_name: Integral Lefschetz algebra / image of U(sl₂) acting on the universal Lefschetz module; representing object for Lefschetz structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: The sl₂ / primitive decomposition viewpoint is classical (Lefschetz, Hodge, Chern, Weil); the motivic usage goes back to Kleiman 1968 and later André and Kahn
ideas.where_published: Not in 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969) in this form, as far as I know

ideas.what: Equivalence: Λ lies in the ring E of (algebraic) correspondences iff the inverses of L^{n-i}: H^i→H^{2n-i} lie in E, given that the Künneth projectors lie in E. Also uniqueness of Λ given L and the grading.
ideas.modern_name: Equivalent forms of the Lefschetz standard conjecture B(X) (Λ algebraic ⇔ inverse of hard Lefschetz algebraic)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck 1968/69 (Standard conjectures); Kleiman 1968 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures'
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay 1968, publ. 1969); expounded by Kleiman (1968)

ideas.what: Counterexample remark (next page): L alone, without the π_i, does not determine a homomorphism from Φ, already for n=1 since Z[L] = Z+ZL
ideas.modern_name: Need for Künneth projectors (conjecture C) alongside L

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates Lefschetz structures integrally and functorially: a Lefschetz structure on a graded ring of correspondences is a ring map from a fixed universal Z-algebra 𝔏 ≅ ∏ M_{n-i+1}(Z). Conjecture B then becomes the extendability of a map defined on L_0 and the π_i. This representing-object viewpoint over Z, rather than Q-linear sl₂ actions, is not how the published literature phrases it.
missed.quote: Il existe un homom. φ: 𝔏 → 𝓔 appliquant L_0 en L, et les π_i en π_i ... De plus, sous ces conditions, l'homo φ des (ii) est unique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a small framing point relevant to integral or torsion versions of the Lefschetz standard conjecture and to motives with integral coefficients. Mathematically it is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the known equivalence of forms of standard conjecture B, as later written up by Kleiman, recast as a universal-algebra statement over Z with a matrix-unit ring. The packaging is a nice unpublished detail, but it is mathematically routine and not a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'Résulte de l'unicité [?] des multiplications' should likely read 'Résulte de la table des multiplications des φ_i^{β,α} donnée au n° 6, et du th. donné au n° 6'.

Line 5: 'il transforme Λ_0 en Λ, les π_{iα} en' continues on the next line with 'π_{iα}' (the printed 'π_i en π_i' seems to belong to a separate item). The final clause is 'φ_i^{β,α} en φ_i^{β,α}', with the subscript/superscript placement as in the image.
Second line of the page: '(des π_i ∈ Σ)' is a plausible reading of '(des π_i [?] Σ)'.

Near the bottom: 'Pour l'unicité de φ, il suffit de voir que φ(Λ)=Λ, et que φ(π_{i,α}) = π_{i,α}, ce qui résulte simultanément ... des formules (6.14)'. The equation number could also be (6.11); it is hard to read.
